intro: Professionals and everyday users convert joules (J) to foot-pounds (ft·lbf) when working across si and imperial standards in residential electricity billing, HVAC heating load calculations, battery storage sizing, and nutritional energy tracking. One joule equals 0.737562 foot-pounds, while 1 foot-pound (ft·lbf) equals 1.355818 joules. Whether you are verifying energy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Joule to Foot-pound (ft·lbf) is 0.73756215, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many foot-pounds (ft·lbf) are in 1 joule (J)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.73756215 foot-pounds (ft·lbf) in 1 joule (J), which rounds to 0.7376 ft·lbf for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 foot-pound (ft·lbf) equals 1.355818 joules.

faqs.question: How do I convert joules to foot-pounds (J to ft·lbf)?
faqs.answer: To convert joules to foot-pounds, use the formula: ft·lbf = J × 0.73756215. For example, converting 500 J gives 368.7811 ft·lbf.

faqs.question: What is 500 joules in foot-pounds?
faqs.answer: 500 joules (J) equals exactly 368.7811 foot-pounds (ft·lbf) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
